units.leftText: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):
units.rightText: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):

units.leftText: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
units.rightText: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,

units.leftText: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
units.rightText: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,

units.leftText: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
units.rightText: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

units.leftText: All the souls who came out of Jacob’s body were seventy souls, and Joseph was in Egypt already.
units.rightText: And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: and Joseph was in Egypt already.

units.leftText: Joseph died, as did all his brothers, and all that generation.
units.rightText: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

units.leftText: The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.

units.leftText: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who didn’t know Joseph.
units.rightText: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph.

units.leftText: He said to his people, “Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.
units.rightText: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:
leftNotes: 1:9 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Come, let’s deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when any war breaks out, they also join themselves to our enemies and fight against us, and escape out of the land.”
units.rightText: come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they also join themselves unto our enemies, and fight against us, and get them up out of the land.

units.leftText: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens. They built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.
units.rightText: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pithom and Raamses.

units.leftText: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread out. They started to dread the children of Israel.
units.rightText: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
units.rightText: And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigor:

units.leftText: and they made their lives bitter with hard service in mortar and in brick, and in all kinds of service in the field, all their service, in which they ruthlessly made them serve.
units.rightText: and they made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field, all their service, wherein they made them serve with rigor.

units.leftText: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah,
units.rightText: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:

units.leftText: and he said, “When you perform the duty of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them on the birth stool, if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.”
units.rightText: and he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the birth-stool; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him; but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.

units.leftText: But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the baby boys alive.
units.rightText: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men-children alive.
leftNotes: 1:17 The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים*” (Elohim).

units.leftText: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them, “Why have you done this thing and saved the boys alive?”
units.rightText: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men-children alive?

units.leftText: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women aren’t like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife comes to them.”
units.rightText: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwife come unto them.

units.leftText: God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied, and grew very mighty.
units.rightText: And God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.

units.leftText: Because the midwives feared God, he gave them families.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them households.

units.leftText: Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “You shall cast every son who is born into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.

units.leftText: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.
units.rightText: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.

units.leftText: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.
units.rightText: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

units.leftText: When she could no longer hide him, she took a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She put the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the river’s bank.
units.rightText: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch; and she put the child therein, and laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

units.leftText: His sister stood far off, to see what would be done to him.
units.rightText: And his sister stood afar off, to know what would be done to him.

units.leftText: Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe at the river. Her maidens walked along by the riverside. She saw the basket among the reeds, and sent her servant to get it.
units.rightText: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river-side; and she saw the ark among the flags, and sent her handmaid to fetch it.

units.leftText: She opened it, and saw the child, and behold, the baby cried. She had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”
units.rightText: And she opened it, and saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

units.leftText: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Should I go and call a nurse for you from the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?”
units.rightText: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?

units.leftText: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Go.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maiden went and called the child’s mother.

units.leftText: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child away, and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.

units.leftText: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”
units.rightText: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, and said, Because I drew him out of the water.
leftNotes: 2:10 “Moses” sounds like the Hebrew for “draw out”.

units.leftText: In those days, when Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers and saw their burdens. He saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown up, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he saw an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his brethren.

units.leftText: He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no one, he killed the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
units.rightText: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he smote the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.

units.leftText: He went out the second day, and behold, two men of the Hebrews were fighting with each other. He said to him who did the wrong, “Why do you strike your fellow?”
units.rightText: And he went out the second day, and, behold, two men of the Hebrews were striving together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?

units.leftText: He said, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian?”
units.rightText: And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? thinkest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely the thing is known.

units.leftText: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and lived in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well.
units.rightText: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

units.leftText: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
units.rightText: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.

units.leftText: The shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
units.rightText: And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.

units.leftText: When they came to Reuel, their father, he said, “How is it that you have returned so early today?”
units.rightText: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to-day?

units.leftText: They said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock.”
units.rightText: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock.

units.leftText: He said to his daughters, “Where is he? Why is it that you have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.”
units.rightText: And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that ye have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.

units.leftText: Moses was content to dwell with the man. He gave Moses Zipporah, his daughter.
units.rightText: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

units.leftText: She bore a son, and he named him Gershom, for he said, “I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land.”
units.rightText: And she bare a son, and he called his name Gershom; for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.
leftNotes: 2:22 “Gershom” sounds like the Hebrew for “an alien there”.

units.leftText: In the course of those many days, the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up to God because of the bondage.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.

units.leftText: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
units.rightText: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

units.leftText: God saw the children of Israel, and God understood.
units.rightText: And God saw the children of Israel, and God took knowledge of them.

units.leftText: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to God’s mountain, to Horeb.
units.rightText: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to the mountain of God, unto Horeb.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the middle of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
leftNotes: 3:2 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: Moses said, “I will go now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burned.”
units.rightText: And Moses said, I will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.

units.leftText: When the LORD saw that he came over to see, God called to him out of the middle of the bush, and said, “Moses! Moses!”
units.rightText: And when Jehovah saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: He said, “Don’t come close. Take off your sandals, for the place you are standing on is holy ground.”
units.rightText: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

units.leftText: Moreover he said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.”
units.rightText: Moreover he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.

units.leftText: The LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people that are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;

units.leftText: I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
units.rightText: and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

units.leftText: Now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
units.rightText: And now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: moreover I have seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.

units.leftText: Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt.”
units.rightText: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.

units.leftText: Moses said to God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?

units.leftText: He said, “Certainly I will be with you. This will be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”
units.rightText: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be the token unto thee, that I have sent thee: when thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.

units.leftText: Moses said to God, “Behold, when I come to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is his name?’ what should I tell them?”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? What shall I say unto them?

units.leftText: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
units.rightText: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

units.leftText: God said moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the children of Israel this, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.
units.rightText: And God said moreover unto Moses, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
leftNotes: 3:15 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: Go and gather the elders of Israel together, and tell them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt.
units.rightText: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, Jehovah, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, hath appeared unto me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt:

units.leftText: I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.”’
units.rightText: and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt unto the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.

units.leftText: They will listen to your voice. You shall come, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall tell him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD, our God.’
units.rightText: And they shall hearken to thy voice: and thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye shall say unto him, Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, hath met with us: and now let us go, we pray thee, three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Jehovah our God.

units.leftText: I know that the king of Egypt won’t give you permission to go, no, not by a mighty hand.
units.rightText: And I know that the king of Egypt will not give you leave to go, no, not by a mighty hand.

units.leftText: I will reach out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders which I will do among them, and after that he will let you go.
units.rightText: And I will put forth my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.

units.leftText: I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and it will happen that when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.
units.rightText: And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty.

units.leftText: But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her who visits her house, jewels of silver, jewels of gold, and clothing. You shall put them on your sons, and on your daughters. You shall plunder the Egyptians.”
units.rightText: But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her that sojourneth in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment: and ye shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters; and ye shall despoil the Egyptians.

units.leftText: Moses answered, “But, behold, they will not believe me, nor listen to my voice; for they will say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’”
units.rightText: And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice; for they will say, Jehovah hath not appeared unto thee.

units.leftText: The LORD said to him, “What is that in your hand?”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, What is that in thy hand? And he said, A rod.

units.leftText: He said, “Throw it on the ground.”
units.rightText: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand, and take it by the tail.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Put forth thy hand, and take it by the tail: (and he put forth his hand, and laid hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand);

units.leftText: “This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.”
units.rightText: that they may believe that Jehovah, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.

units.leftText: The LORD said furthermore to him, “Now put your hand inside your cloak.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said furthermore unto him, Put now thy hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous, as white as snow.

units.leftText: He said, “Put your hand inside your cloak again.”
units.rightText: And he said, Put thy hand into thy bosom again. (And he put his hand into his bosom again; and when he took it out of his bosom, behold, it was turned again as his other flesh.)

units.leftText: “It will happen, if they will not believe you or listen to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.

units.leftText: It will happen, if they will not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, that you shall take of the water of the river, and pour it on the dry land. The water which you take out of the river will become blood on the dry land.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe even these two signs, neither hearken unto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river, and pour it upon the dry land: and the water which thou takest out of the river shall become blood upon the dry land.

units.leftText: Moses said to the LORD, “O Lord, I am not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Jehovah, Oh, Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
leftNotes: 4:10 The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai”.

units.leftText: The LORD said to him, “Who made man’s mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Isn’t it I, the LORD?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh a man dumb, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? is it not I, Jehovah?

units.leftText: Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.”
units.rightText: Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt speak.

units.leftText: Moses said, “Oh, Lord, please send someone else.”
units.rightText: And he said, Oh, Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.

units.leftText: The LORD’s anger burned against Moses, and he said, “What about Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Also, behold, he is coming out to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is there not Aaron thy brother the Levite? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.

units.leftText: You shall speak to him, and put the words in his mouth. I will be with your mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what you shall do.
units.rightText: And thou shalt speak unto him, and put the words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.

units.leftText: He will be your spokesman to the people. It will happen that he will be to you a mouth, and you will be to him as God.
units.rightText: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people; and it shall come to pass, that he shall be to thee a mouth, and thou shalt be to him as God.

units.leftText: You shall take this rod in your hand, with which you shall do the signs.”
units.rightText: And thou shalt take in thy hand this rod, wherewith thou shalt do the signs.

units.leftText: Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said to him, “Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still alive.”
units.rightText: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said unto him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren that are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses in Midian, “Go, return into Egypt; for all the men who sought your life are dead.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt; for all the men are dead that sought thy life.

units.leftText: Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Egypt. Moses took God’s rod in his hand.
units.rightText: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of God in his hand.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “When you go back into Egypt, see that you do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in your hand, but I will harden his heart and he will not let the people go.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, When thou goest back into Egypt, see that thou do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in thy hand: but I will harden his heart and he will not let the people go.

units.leftText: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘The LORD says, Israel is my son, my firstborn,
units.rightText: And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, Israel is my son, my first-born:

units.leftText: and I have said to you, “Let my son go, that he may serve me;” and you have refused to let him go. Behold, I will kill your firstborn son.’”
units.rightText: and I have said unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me; and thou hast refused to let him go: behold, I will slay thy son, thy first-born.

units.leftText: On the way at a lodging place, the LORD met Moses and wanted to kill him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the way at the lodging-place, that Jehovah met him, and sought to kill him.

units.leftText: Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said, “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me.”
units.rightText: Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said, Surely a bridegroom of blood art thou to me.

units.leftText: So he let him alone. Then she said, “You are a bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision.
units.rightText: So he let him alone. Then she said, A bridegroom of blood art thou, because of the circumcision.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Aaron, “Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.

units.leftText: Moses told Aaron all the LORD’s words with which he had sent him, and all the signs with which he had instructed him.
units.rightText: And Moses told Aaron all the words of Jehovah wherewith he had sent him, and all the signs wherewith he had charged him.

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they had not grown up.
units.rightText: But the wheat and the spelt were not smitten: for they were not grown up.

units.rightText: And Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread abroad his hands unto Jehovah: and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured upon the earth.

units.rightText: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto Jehovah.

units.rightText: And he said unto them, So be Jehovah with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones: look to it; for evil is before you.

units.rightText: Not so: go now ye that are men, and serve Jehovah; for that is what ye desire. And they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail hath left.

units.rightText: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and Jehovah brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all the night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.

units.rightText: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the borders of Egypt; very grievous were they; before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such.

units.rightText: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste; and he said, I have sinned against Jehovah your God, and against you.

units.rightText: and ye shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at even.

units.leftText: They shall take some of the blood, and put it on the two door posts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they shall eat it.
units.rightText: And they shall take of the blood, and put it on the two side-posts and on the lintel, upon the houses wherein they shall eat it.

units.leftText: They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, with unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.
units.rightText: And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; with bitter herbs they shall eat it.

units.leftText: Don’t eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with fire; with its head, its legs and its inner parts.
units.rightText: Eat not of it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roast with fire; its head with its legs and with the inwards thereof.

units.leftText: You shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remains of it until the morning you shall burn with fire.
units.rightText: And ye shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remaineth of it until the morning ye shall burn with fire.

units.leftText: This is how you shall eat it: with your belt on your waist, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD’s Passover.
units.rightText: And thus shall ye eat it: with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is Jehovah’s passover.

units.leftText: For I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will strike all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and animal. I will execute judgments against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
units.rightText: For I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will smite all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and there shall no plague be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall keep it as a feast to the LORD. You shall keep it as a feast throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.
units.rightText: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial, and ye shall keep it a feast to Jehovah: throughout your generations ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

units.leftText: “‘Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; even the first day you shall put away yeast out of your houses, for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
units.rightText: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.

units.leftText: In the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no kind of work shall be done in them, except that which every man must eat, only that may be done by you.
units.rightText: And in the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no manner of work shall be done in them, save that which every man must eat, that only may be done by you.

units.leftText: You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this same day I have brought your armies out of the land of Egypt. Therefore you shall observe this day throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.
units.rightText: And ye shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this selfsame day have I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt: therefore shall ye observe this day throughout your generations by an ordinance for ever.

units.leftText: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty first day of the month at evening.
units.rightText: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.

units.leftText: There shall be no yeast found in your houses for seven days, for whoever eats that which is leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he is a foreigner, or one who is born in the land.
units.rightText: Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whosoever eateth that which is leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a sojourner, or one that is born in the land.

units.leftText: You shall eat nothing leavened. In all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread.’”
units.rightText: Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread.

units.leftText: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said to them, “Draw out, and take lambs according to your families, and kill the Passover.
units.rightText: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out, and take you lambs according to your families, and kill the passover.

units.leftText: You shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two door posts with the blood that is in the basin. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.
units.rightText: And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two side-posts with the blood that is in the basin; and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.

units.leftText: For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, and on the two door posts, the LORD will pass over the door, and will not allow the destroyer to come in to your houses to strike you.
units.rightText: For Jehovah will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side-posts, Jehovah will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.

units.leftText: You shall observe this thing for an ordinance to you and to your sons forever.
units.rightText: And ye shall observe this thing for an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever.

units.leftText: It shall happen when you have come to the land which the LORD will give you, as he has promised, that you shall keep this service.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when ye are come to the land which Jehovah will give you, according as he hath promised, that ye shall keep this service.

units.leftText: It will happen, when your children ask you, ‘What do you mean by this service?’
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service?

units.leftText: that you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of the LORD’s Passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, and spared our houses.’”
units.rightText: that ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of Jehovah’s passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.

units.leftText: The children of Israel went and did so; as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel went and did so; as Jehovah had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

units.leftText: At midnight, the LORD struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of livestock.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at midnight, that Jehovah smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the first-born of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the first-born of cattle.

units.leftText: Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

units.leftText: He called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, “Rise up, get out from among my people, both you and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD, as you have said!
units.rightText: And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve Jehovah, as ye have said.

units.leftText: Take both your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone; and bless me also!”
units.rightText: Take both your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also.

units.leftText: The Egyptians were urgent with the people, to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, “We are all dead men.”
units.rightText: And the Egyptians were urgent upon the people, to send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We are all dead men.

units.leftText: The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs being bound up in their clothes on their shoulders.
units.rightText: And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading-troughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.

units.leftText: The children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they asked of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they asked of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment:

units.leftText: The LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. They plundered the Egyptians.
units.rightText: and Jehovah gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. And they despoiled the Egyptians.

units.leftText: The children of Israel traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot who were men, in addition to children.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, besides children.

units.leftText: A mixed multitude went up also with them, with flocks, herds, and even very much livestock.
units.rightText: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.

units.leftText: They baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought out of Egypt; for it wasn’t leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and couldn’t wait, and they had not prepared any food for themselves.
units.rightText: And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth out of Egypt; for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victuals.

units.leftText: Now the time that the children of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
units.rightText: Now the time that the children of Israel dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.

units.leftText: At the end of four hundred thirty years, to the day, all of the LORD’s armies went out from the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Jehovah went out from the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: It is a night to be much observed to the LORD for bringing them out from the land of Egypt. This is that night of the LORD, to be much observed by all the children of Israel throughout their generations.
units.rightText: It is a night to be much observed unto Jehovah for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is that night of Jehovah, to be much observed of all the children of Israel throughout their generations.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance of the Passover. No foreigner shall eat of it,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses and Aaron, This is the ordinance of the passover: there shall no foreigner eat thereof;

units.leftText: but every man’s servant who is bought for money, when you have circumcised him, then shall he eat of it.
units.rightText: but every man’s servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat thereof.

units.leftText: A foreigner and a hired servant shall not eat of it.
units.rightText: A sojourner and a hired servant shall not eat thereof.

units.leftText: It must be eaten in one house. You shall not carry any of the meat outside of the house. Do not break any of its bones.
units.rightText: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth aught of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.

units.leftText: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.
units.rightText: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

units.leftText: When a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, and would like to keep the Passover to the LORD, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it. He shall be as one who is born in the land; but no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
units.rightText: And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to Jehovah, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: but no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.

units.leftText: One law shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you.”
units.rightText: One law shall be to him that is home-born, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you.

units.leftText: All the children of Israel did so. As the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
units.rightText: Thus did all the children of Israel; as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

units.leftText: That same day, the LORD brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.
units.rightText: And it came to pass the selfsame day, that Jehovah did bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their hosts.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Sanctify to me all the firstborn, whatever opens the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of animal. It is mine.”
units.rightText: Sanctify unto me all the first-born, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.

units.leftText: Moses said to the people, “Remember this day, in which you came out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from this place. No leavened bread shall be eaten.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand Jehovah brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.

units.leftText: Today you go out in the month Abib.
units.rightText: This day ye go forth in the month Abib.

units.leftText: It shall be, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall keep this service in this month.
units.rightText: And it shall be, when Jehovah shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.

units.leftText: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to the LORD.
units.rightText: Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; and no leavened bread shall be seen with you. No yeast shall be seen with you, within all your borders.
units.rightText: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee, in all thy borders.

units.leftText: You shall tell your son in that day, saying, ‘It is because of that which the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
units.rightText: And thou shalt tell thy son in that day, saying, It is because of that which Jehovah did for me when I came forth out of Egypt.

units.leftText: It shall be for a sign to you on your hand, and for a memorial between your eyes, that the LORD’s law may be in your mouth; for with a strong hand the LORD has brought you out of Egypt.
units.rightText: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thy hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the law of Jehovah may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath Jehovah brought thee out of Egypt.

units.leftText: You shall therefore keep this ordinance in its season from year to year.
units.rightText: Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in its season from year to year.

units.leftText: “It shall be, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your fathers, and will give it to you,
units.rightText: And it shall be, when Jehovah shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanite, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,

units.leftText: that you shall set apart to the LORD all that opens the womb, and every firstborn that comes from an animal which you have. The males shall be the LORD’s.
units.rightText: that thou shalt set apart unto Jehovah all that openeth the womb, and every firstling which thou hast that cometh of a beast; the males shall be Jehovah’s.

units.leftText: Every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck; and you shall redeem all the firstborn of man among your sons.
units.rightText: And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break its neck: and all the first-born of man among thy sons shalt thou redeem.

units.leftText: It shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ that you shall tell him, ‘By strength of hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage.
units.rightText: And it shall be, when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say unto him, By strength of hand Jehovah brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage:

units.leftText: When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of livestock. Therefore I sacrifice to the LORD all that opens the womb, being males; but all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.’
units.rightText: and it came to pass, when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, that Jehovah slew all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both the first-born of man, and the first-born of beast: therefore I sacrifice to Jehovah all that openeth the womb, being males; but all the first-born of my sons I redeem.

units.leftText: It shall be for a sign on your hand, and for symbols between your eyes; for by strength of hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.”
units.rightText: And it shall be for a sign upon thy hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand Jehovah brought us forth out of Egypt.

units.leftText: When Pharaoh had let the people go, God didn’t lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, “Lest perhaps the people change their minds when they see war, and they return to Egypt”;
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:

units.leftText: but God led the people around by the way of the wilderness by the Red Sea; and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: but God led the people about, by the way of the wilderness by the Red Sea: and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had made the children of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones away from here with you.”
units.rightText: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

units.leftText: They took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.
units.rightText: And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.

units.leftText: The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light, that they might go by day and by night:
units.rightText: And Jehovah went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; that they might go by day and by night:

units.leftText: the pillar of cloud by day, and the pillar of fire by night, didn’t depart from before the people.
units.rightText: the pillar of cloud by day, and the pillar of fire by night, departed not from before the people.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Zephon. You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-zephon: over against it shall ye encamp by the sea.

units.leftText: Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, ‘They are entangled in the land. The wilderness has shut them in.’
units.rightText: And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the wilderness hath shut them in.

units.leftText: I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will follow after them; and I will get honor over Pharaoh, and over all his armies; and the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD.” They did so.
units.rightText: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he shall follow after them; and I will get me honor upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host: and the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah. And they did so.

units.leftText: The king of Egypt was told that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed toward the people, and they said, “What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?”
units.rightText: And it was told the king of Egypt that the people were fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed towards the people, and they said, What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?

units.leftText: He prepared his chariot, and took his army with him;
units.rightText: And he made ready his chariot, and took his people with him:

units.leftText: and he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, with captains over all of them.
units.rightText: and he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over all of them.

units.leftText: The LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the children of Israel; for the children of Israel went out with a high hand.
units.rightText: And Jehovah hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel: for the children of Israel went out with a high hand.

units.leftText: The Egyptians pursued them. All the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, his horsemen, and his army overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pihahiroth, before Baal Zephon.
units.rightText: And the Egyptians pursued after them, all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.

units.leftText: When Pharaoh came near, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were very afraid. The children of Israel cried out to the LORD.
units.rightText: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: They said to Moses, “Because there were no graves in Egypt, have you taken us away to die in the wilderness? Why have you treated us this way, to bring us out of Egypt?
units.rightText: And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to bring us forth out of Egypt?

units.leftText: Isn’t this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
units.rightText: Is not this the word that we spake unto thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it were better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will work for you today; for you will never again see the Egyptians whom you have seen today.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Jehovah, which he will work for you to-day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to-day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.

units.leftText: The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be still.”
units.rightText: Jehovah will fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Why do you cry to me? Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward.

units.leftText: Lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it. Then the children of Israel shall go into the middle of the sea on dry ground.
units.rightText: And lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thy hand over the sea, and divide it: and the children of Israel shall go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.

units.leftText: Behold, I myself will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they will go in after them. I will get myself honor over Pharaoh, and over all his armies, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.
units.rightText: And I, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall go in after them: and I will get me honor upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

units.leftText: The Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD when I have gotten myself honor over Pharaoh, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.”
units.rightText: And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I have gotten me honor upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

units.leftText: The angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud moved from before them, and stood behind them.
units.rightText: And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud removed from before them, and stood behind them:

units.rightText: and it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, yet gave it light by night: and the one came not near the other all the night.

units.rightText: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and Jehovah caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all the night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

units.leftText: The children of Israel went into the middle of the sea on the dry ground; and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

units.leftText: The Egyptians pursued, and went in after them into the middle of the sea: all of Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.
units.rightText: And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them into the midst of the sea, all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

units.leftText: In the morning watch, the LORD looked out on the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and confused the Egyptian army.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning watch, that Jehovah looked forth upon the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and discomfited the host of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: He took off their chariot wheels, and they drove them heavily; so that the Egyptians said, “Let’s flee from the face of Israel, for the LORD fights for them against the Egyptians!”
units.rightText: And he took off their chariot wheels, and they drove them heavily; so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for Jehovah fighteth for them against the Egyptians.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may come again on the Egyptians, on their chariots, and on their horsemen.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Stretch out thy hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.

units.leftText: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it. The LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.
units.rightText: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Jehovah overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

units.leftText: The waters returned, and covered the chariots and the horsemen, even all Pharaoh’s army that went in after them into the sea. There remained not so much as one of them.
units.rightText: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, even all the host of Pharaoh that went in after them into the sea; there remained not so much as one of them.

units.leftText: But the children of Israel walked on dry land in the middle of the sea, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
units.rightText: But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea; and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

units.leftText: Thus the LORD saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
units.rightText: Thus Jehovah saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea-shore.

units.leftText: Israel saw the great work which the LORD did to the Egyptians, and the people feared the LORD; and they believed in the LORD and in his servant Moses.
units.rightText: And Israel saw the great work which Jehovah did upon the Egyptians, and the people feared Jehovah: and they believed in Jehovah, and in his servant Moses.

units.leftText: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the LORD, and said,
units.rightText: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto Jehovah, and spake, saying,
leftNotes: 15:1 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: The LORD is my strength and song.
units.rightText: Jehovah is my strength and song,
leftNotes: 15:2 Hebrew: יה Yah

units.leftText: The LORD is a man of war.
units.rightText: Jehovah is a man of war:

units.leftText: He has cast Pharaoh’s chariots and his army into the sea.
units.rightText: Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea;

units.leftText: The deeps cover them.
units.rightText: The deeps cover them:

units.leftText: Your right hand, LORD, is glorious in power.
units.rightText: Thy right hand, O Jehovah, is glorious in power,

units.leftText: In the greatness of your excellency, you overthrow those who rise up against you.
units.rightText: And in the greatness of thine excellency thou overthrowest them that rise up against thee:

units.leftText: With the blast of your nostrils, the waters were piled up.
units.rightText: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were piled up,

units.leftText: The enemy said, ‘I will pursue. I will overtake. I will divide the plunder.
units.rightText: The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil;

units.leftText: You blew with your wind.
units.rightText: Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them:

units.leftText: Who is like you, LORD, among the gods?
units.rightText: Who is like unto thee, O Jehovah, among the gods?

units.leftText: You stretched out your right hand.
units.rightText: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand,

units.leftText: “You, in your loving kindness, have led the people that you have redeemed.
units.rightText: Thou in thy lovingkindness hast led the people that thou hast redeemed:

units.leftText: The peoples have heard.
units.rightText: The peoples have heard, they tremble:

units.leftText: Then the chiefs of Edom were dismayed.
units.rightText: Then were the chiefs of Edom dismayed;

units.leftText: Terror and dread falls on them.
units.rightText: Terror and dread falleth upon them;

units.leftText: You will bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of your inheritance,
units.rightText: Thou wilt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance,

units.leftText: The LORD will reign forever and ever.”
units.rightText: Jehovah shall reign for ever and ever.

units.leftText: For the horses of Pharaoh went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and the LORD brought back the waters of the sea on them; but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the middle of the sea.
units.rightText: For the horses of Pharaoh went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and Jehovah brought back the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea.

units.leftText: Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand; and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.
units.rightText: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.

units.leftText: Miriam answered them,
units.rightText: And Miriam answered them,

units.leftText: Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
units.rightText: And Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.

units.leftText: When they came to Marah, they couldn’t drink from the waters of Marah, for they were bitter. Therefore its name was called Marah.
units.rightText: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah.
leftNotes: 15:23 Marah means bitter.

units.leftText: The people murmured against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”
units.rightText: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?

units.leftText: Then he cried to the LORD. The LORD showed him a tree, and he threw it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet. There he made a statute and an ordinance for them, and there he tested them.
units.rightText: And he cried unto Jehovah; and Jehovah showed him a tree, and he cast it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet. There he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them;

units.leftText: He said, “If you will diligently listen to the LORD your God’s voice, and will do that which is right in his eyes, and will pay attention to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have put on the Egyptians; for I am the LORD who heals you.”
units.rightText: and he said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his eyes, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases upon thee, which I have put upon the Egyptians: for I am Jehovah that healeth thee.

units.leftText: They came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They encamped there by the waters.
units.rightText: And they came to Elim, where were twelve springs of water, and threescore and ten palm-trees: and they encamped there by the waters.

units.leftText: They took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: The whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness;
units.rightText: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness:

units.leftText: and the children of Israel said to them, “We wish that we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the meat pots, when we ate our fill of bread, for you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”
units.rightText: and the children of Israel said unto them, Would that we had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh-pots, when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not.
units.rightText: Then said Jehovah unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or not.

units.leftText: It shall come to pass on the sixth day, that they shall prepare that which they bring in, and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass on the sixth day, that they shall prepare that which they bring in, and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily.

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel, “At evening, you shall know that the LORD has brought you out from the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron said unto all the children of Israel, At even, then ye shall know that Jehovah hath brought you out from the land of Egypt;

units.leftText: In the morning, you shall see the LORD’s glory; because he hears your murmurings against the LORD. Who are we, that you murmur against us?”
units.rightText: and in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of Jehovah; for that he heareth your murmurings against Jehovah: and what are we, that ye murmur against us?

units.leftText: Moses said, “Now the LORD will give you meat to eat in the evening, and in the morning bread to satisfy you, because the LORD hears your murmurings which you murmur against him. And who are we? Your murmurings are not against us, but against the LORD.”
units.rightText: And Moses said, This shall be, when Jehovah shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for that Jehovah heareth your murmurings which ye murmur against him: and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against Jehovah.

units.leftText: Moses said to Aaron, “Tell all the congregation of the children of Israel, ‘Come close to the LORD, for he has heard your murmurings.’”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Aaron, Say unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before Jehovah; for he hath heard your murmurings.

units.leftText: As Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the children of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the LORD’s glory appeared in the cloud.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as Aaron spake unto the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that they looked toward the wilderness, and, behold, the glory of Jehovah appeared in the cloud.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel. Speak to them, saying, ‘At evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
units.rightText: I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel: speak unto them, saying, At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread: and ye shall know that I am Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: In the evening, quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at even, that the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the camp.

units.leftText: When the dew that lay had gone, behold, on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
units.rightText: And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness a small round thing, small as the hoar-frost on the ground.

units.leftText: When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they didn’t know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread which the LORD has given you to eat.
units.rightText: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, What is it? for they knew not what it was. And Moses said unto them, It is the bread which Jehovah hath given you to eat.

units.leftText: This is the thing which the LORD has commanded: ‘Gather of it everyone according to his eating; an omer a head, according to the number of your persons, you shall take it, every man for those who are in his tent.’”
units.rightText: This is the thing which Jehovah hath commanded, Gather ye of it every man according to his eating; an omer a head, according to the number of your persons, shall ye take it, every man for them that are in his tent.
leftNotes: 16:16 An omer is about 2.2 liters or about 2.3 quarts

units.leftText: The children of Israel did so, and some gathered more, some less.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did so, and gathered some more, some less.

units.leftText: When they measured it with an omer, he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack. They each gathered according to his eating.
units.rightText: And when they measured it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.

units.leftText: Moses said to them, “Let no one leave of it until the morning.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto them, Let no man leave of it till the morning.

units.leftText: Notwithstanding they didn’t listen to Moses, but some of them left of it until the morning, so it bred worms and became foul; and Moses was angry with them.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and became foul: and Moses was wroth with them.

units.leftText: They gathered it morning by morning, everyone according to his eating. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
units.rightText: And they gathered it morning by morning, every man according to his eating: and when the sun waxed hot, it melted.

units.leftText: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each one; and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each one: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.

units.leftText: He said to them, “This is that which the LORD has spoken, ‘Tomorrow is a solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. Bake that which you want to bake, and boil that which you want to boil; and all that remains over lay up for yourselves to be kept until the morning.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, This is that which Jehovah hath spoken, To-morrow is a solemn rest, a holy sabbath unto Jehovah: bake that which ye will bake, and boil that which ye will boil; and all that remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.

units.leftText: They laid it up until the morning, as Moses ordered, and it didn’t become foul, and there were no worms in it.
units.rightText: And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not become foul, neither was there any worm therein.

units.leftText: Moses said, “Eat that today, for today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you shall not find it in the field.
units.rightText: And Moses said, Eat that to-day; for to-day is a sabbath unto Jehovah: to-day ye shall not find it in the field.

units.leftText: Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day is the Sabbath. In it there shall be none.”
units.rightText: Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.

units.leftText: On the seventh day, some of the people went out to gather, and they found none.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that there went out some of the people to gather, and they found none.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “How long do you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?

units.leftText: Behold, because the LORD has given you the Sabbath, therefore he gives you on the sixth day the bread of two days. Everyone stay in his place. Let no one go out of his place on the seventh day.”
units.rightText: See, for that Jehovah hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.

units.leftText: So the people rested on the seventh day.
units.rightText: So the people rested on the seventh day.
