units.leftText: The house of Israel called its name “Manna”, and it was like coriander seed, white; and its taste was like wafers with honey.
units.rightText: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.
leftNotes: 16:31 “Manna” means “What is it?”

units.leftText: Moses said, “This is the thing which the LORD has commanded, ‘Let an omer-full of it be kept throughout your generations, that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
units.rightText: And Moses said, This is the thing which Jehovah hath commanded, Let an omerful of it be kept throughout your generations, that they may see the bread wherewith I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Moses said to Aaron, “Take a pot, and put an omer-full of manna in it, and lay it up before the LORD, to be kept throughout your generations.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omerful of manna therein, and lay it up before Jehovah, to be kept throughout your generations.

units.leftText: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
units.rightText: As Jehovah commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.

units.leftText: The children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate the manna until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did eat the manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat the manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Now an omer is one tenth of an ephah.
units.rightText: Now an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.
leftNotes: 16:36 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel

units.leftText: All the congregation of the children of Israel traveled from the wilderness of Sin, starting according to the LORD’s commandment, and encamped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
units.rightText: And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, by their journeys, according to the commandment of Jehovah, and encamped in Rephidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.

units.leftText: Therefore the people quarreled with Moses, and said, “Give us water to drink.”
units.rightText: Wherefore the people strove with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why strive ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt Jehovah?

units.leftText: The people were thirsty for water there; so the people murmured against Moses, and said, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?”
units.rightText: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore hast thou brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?

units.leftText: Moses cried to the LORD, saying, “What shall I do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me.”
units.rightText: And Moses cried unto Jehovah, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they are almost ready to stone me.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Walk on before the people, and take the elders of Israel with you, and take the rod in your hand with which you struck the Nile, and go.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pass on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thy hand, and go.

units.leftText: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock in Horeb. You shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, that the people may drink.” Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
units.rightText: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.

units.leftText: He called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because the children of Israel quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us, or not?”
units.rightText: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the striving of the children of Israel, and because they tempted Jehovah, saying, Is Jehovah among us, or not?
leftNotes: 17:7 Massah means testing.
17:7 Meribah means quarreling.

units.leftText: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
units.rightText: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

units.leftText: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose men for us, and go out to fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with God’s rod in my hand.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to-morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in my hand.

units.leftText: So Joshua did as Moses had told him, and fought with Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
units.rightText: So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

units.leftText: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed; and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

units.leftText: But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.
units.rightText: But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.

units.leftText: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
units.rightText: And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky.”
units.rightText: and Jehovah said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.

units.leftText: Moses built an altar, and called its name “The LORD our Banner”.
units.rightText: And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovah-nissi;
leftNotes: 17:15 Or, The LORD Nissi. LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: He said, “The LORD has sworn: ‘The LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.’”
units.rightText: and he said, Jehovah hath sworn: Jehovah will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
leftNotes: 17:16 Hebrew: יה Yah
17:16 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
units.rightText: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, how that Jehovah had brought Israel out of Egypt.

units.leftText: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, received Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after he had sent her away,
units.rightText: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after he had sent her away,

units.leftText: and her two sons. The name of one son was Gershom, for Moses said, “I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land”.
units.rightText: and her two sons; of whom the name of the one was Gershom; for he said, I have been a sojourner in a foreign land:
leftNotes: 18:3 “Gershom” sounds like the Hebrew for “an alien there”.

units.leftText: The name of the other was Eliezer, for he said, “My father’s God was my help and delivered me from Pharaoh’s sword.”
units.rightText: and the name of the other was Eliezer; for he said, The God of my father was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.
leftNotes: 18:4 Eliezer means “God is my helper”.

units.leftText: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with Moses’ sons and his wife to Moses into the wilderness where he was encamped, at the Mountain of God.
units.rightText: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife unto Moses into the wilderness where he was encamped, at the mount of God:

units.leftText: He said to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, have come to you with your wife, and her two sons with her.”
units.rightText: and he said unto Moses, I, thy father-in-law Jethro, am come unto thee, and thy wife, and her two sons with her.

units.leftText: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and bowed and kissed him. They asked each other of their welfare, and they came into the tent.
units.rightText: And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and did obeisance, and kissed him: and they asked each other of their welfare; and they came into the tent.

units.leftText: Moses told his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardships that had come on them on the way, and how the LORD delivered them.
units.rightText: And Moses told his father-in-law all that Jehovah had done unto Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the travail that had come upon them by the way, and how Jehovah delivered them.

units.leftText: Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the LORD had done to Israel, in that he had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians.
units.rightText: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which Jehovah had done to Israel, in that he had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: Jethro said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh; who has delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
units.rightText: And Jethro said, Blessed be Jehovah, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh; who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods because of the way that they treated people arrogantly.”
units.rightText: Now I know that Jehovah is greater than all gods; yea, in the thing wherein they dealt proudly against them.

units.leftText: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron came with all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.
units.rightText: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.

units.leftText: On the next day, Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from the morning to the evening.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood about Moses from the morning unto the evening.

units.leftText: When Moses’ father-in-law saw all that he did to the people, he said, “What is this thing that you do for the people? Why do you sit alone, and all the people stand around you from morning to evening?”
units.rightText: And when Moses’ father-in-law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand about thee from morning unto even?

units.leftText: Moses said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto his father-in-law, Because the people come unto me to inquire of God:

units.leftText: When they have a matter, they come to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.”
units.rightText: when they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.

units.leftText: Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “The thing that you do is not good.
units.rightText: And Moses’ father-in-law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.

units.leftText: You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone.
units.rightText: Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for the thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

units.leftText: Listen now to my voice. I will give you counsel, and God be with you. You represent the people before God, and bring the causes to God.
units.rightText: Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God be with thee: be thou for the people to God-ward, and bring thou the causes unto God:

units.leftText: You shall teach them the statutes and the laws, and shall show them the way in which they must walk, and the work that they must do.
units.rightText: and thou shalt teach them the statutes and the laws, and shalt show them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.

units.leftText: Moreover you shall provide out of all the people able men which fear God: men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
units.rightText: Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:

units.leftText: Let them judge the people at all times. It shall be that every great matter they shall bring to you, but every small matter they shall judge themselves. So shall it be easier for you, and they shall share the load with you.
units.rightText: and let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge themselves: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee.

units.leftText: If you will do this thing, and God commands you so, then you will be able to endure, and all these people also will go to their place in peace.”
units.rightText: If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people also shall go to their place in peace.

units.leftText: So Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said.
units.rightText: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said.

units.leftText: Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
units.rightText: And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

units.leftText: They judged the people at all times. They brought the hard cases to Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.
units.rightText: And they judged the people at all seasons: the hard causes they brought unto Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.

units.leftText: Moses let his father-in-law depart, and he went his way into his own land.
units.rightText: And Moses let his father-in-law depart; and he went his way into his own land.

units.leftText: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that same day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
units.rightText: In the third month after the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they into the wilderness of Sinai.

units.leftText: When they had departed from Rephidim, and had come to the wilderness of Sinai, they encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mountain.
units.rightText: And when they were departed from Rephidim, and were come to the wilderness of Sinai, they encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mount.

units.leftText: Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him out of the mountain, saying, “This is what you shall tell the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:
units.rightText: And Moses went up unto God, and Jehovah called unto him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:

units.leftText: ‘You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to myself.
units.rightText: Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself.

units.leftText: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
units.rightText: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be mine own possession from among all peoples: for all the earth is mine:

units.leftText: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
units.rightText: and ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which the LORD commanded him.
units.rightText: And Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which Jehovah commanded him.

units.leftText: All the people answered together, and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.”
units.rightText: And all the people answered together, and said, All that Jehovah hath spoken we will do. And Moses reported the words of the people unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe you forever.” Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Lo, I come unto thee in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with thee, and may also believe thee for ever. And Moses told the words of the people unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Go unto the people, and sanctify them to-day and to-morrow, and let them wash their garments,

units.leftText: and be ready for the third day; for on the third day the LORD will come down in the sight of all the people on Mount Sinai.
units.rightText: and be ready against the third day; for the third day Jehovah will come down in the sight of all the people upon mount Sinai.

units.leftText: You shall set bounds to the people all around, saying, ‘Be careful that you don’t go up onto the mountain, or touch its border. Whoever touches the mountain shall be surely put to death.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set bounds unto the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, that ye go not up into the mount, or touch the border of it: whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death:

units.leftText: No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether it is animal or man, he shall not live.’ When the trumpet sounds long, they shall come up to the mountain.”
units.rightText: no hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned, or shot through; whether it be beast or man, he shall not live: when the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come up to the mount.

units.leftText: Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their clothes.
units.rightText: And Moses went down from the mount unto the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their garments.

units.leftText: He said to the people, “Be ready by the third day. Don’t have sexual relations with a woman.”
units.rightText: And he said unto the people, Be ready against the third day: come not near a woman.

units.leftText: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of a trumpet exceeding loud; and all the people that were in the camp trembled.

units.leftText: Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the lower part of the mountain.
units.rightText: And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount.

units.leftText: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because the LORD descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
units.rightText: And mount Sinai, the whole of it, smoked, because Jehovah descended upon it in fire; and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly.

units.leftText: When the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him by a voice.
units.rightText: And when the voice of the trumpet waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.

units.leftText: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. The LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
units.rightText: And Jehovah came down upon mount Sinai, to the top of the mount: and Jehovah called Moses to the top of the mount; and Moses went up.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Go down, charge the people, lest they break through unto Jehovah to gaze, and many of them perish.

units.leftText: Let the priests also, who come near to the LORD, sanctify themselves, lest the LORD break out on them.”
units.rightText: And let the priests also, that come near to Jehovah, sanctify themselves, lest Jehovah break forth upon them.

units.leftText: Moses said to the LORD, “The people can’t come up to Mount Sinai, for you warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around the mountain, and sanctify it.’”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Jehovah, The people cannot come up to mount Sinai: for thou didst charge us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.

units.leftText: The LORD said to him, “Go down! You shall bring Aaron up with you, but don’t let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest he break out against them.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Go, get thee down; and thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron with thee: but let not the priests and the people break through to come up unto Jehovah, lest he break forth upon them.

units.leftText: So Moses went down to the people, and told them.
units.rightText: So Moses went down unto the people, and told them.

units.leftText: God spoke all these words, saying,
units.rightText: And God spake all these words, saying,
leftNotes: 20:1 After “God”, the Hebrew has the two letters “Aleph Tav” (the first and last letters of the Hebrew alphabet), not as a word, but as a grammatical marker.

units.leftText: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
units.rightText: I am Jehovah thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

units.leftText: “You shall have no other gods before me.
units.rightText: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

units.leftText: “You shall not make for yourselves an idol, nor any image of anything that is in the heavens above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:
units.rightText: Thou shalt not make unto thee a graven image, nor any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

units.leftText: you shall not bow yourself down to them, nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me,
units.rightText: thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them; for I Jehovah thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation of them that hate me,

units.leftText: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
units.rightText: and showing lovingkindness unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.

units.leftText: “You shall not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not hold him guiltless who misuses his name.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not take the name of Jehovah thy God in vain; for Jehovah will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
leftNotes: 20:7 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.
20:7 or, You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain

units.leftText: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
units.rightText: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

units.leftText: You shall labor six days, and do all your work,
units.rightText: Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work;

units.leftText: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;
units.rightText: but the seventh day is a sabbath unto Jehovah thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

units.leftText: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.
units.rightText: for in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.

units.leftText: “Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.
units.rightText: Honor thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long in the land which Jehovah thy God giveth thee.

units.leftText: “You shall not murder.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not kill.

units.leftText: “You shall not commit adultery.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not commit adultery.

units.leftText: “You shall not steal.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not steal.

units.leftText: “You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.

units.leftText: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
units.rightText: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbor’s.

units.leftText: All the people perceived the thunderings, the lightnings, the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking. When the people saw it, they trembled, and stayed at a distance.
units.rightText: And all the people perceived the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the voice of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw it, they trembled, and stood afar off.

units.leftText: They said to Moses, “Speak with us yourself, and we will listen; but don’t let God speak with us, lest we die.”
units.rightText: And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.

units.leftText: Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid, for God has come to test you, and that his fear may be before you, that you won’t sin.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before you, that ye sin not.

units.leftText: The people stayed at a distance, and Moses came near to the thick darkness where God was.
units.rightText: And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “This is what you shall tell the children of Israel: ‘You yourselves have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Thus thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, Ye yourselves have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.

units.leftText: You shall most certainly not make gods of silver or gods of gold for yourselves to be alongside me.
units.rightText: Ye shall not make other gods with me; gods of silver, or gods of gold, ye shall not make unto you.

units.leftText: You shall make an altar of earth for me, and shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I record my name I will come to you and I will bless you.
units.rightText: An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt-offerings, and thy peace-offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in every place where I record my name I will come unto thee and I will bless thee.

units.leftText: If you make me an altar of stone, you shall not build it of cut stones; for if you lift up your tool on it, you have polluted it.
units.rightText: And if thou make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewn stones; for if thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast polluted it.

units.leftText: You shall not go up by steps to my altar, that your nakedness may not be exposed to it.’
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not uncovered thereon.

units.leftText: “Now these are the ordinances which you shall set before them:
units.rightText: Now these are the ordinances which thou shalt set before them.

units.leftText: “If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go out free without paying anything.
units.rightText: If thou buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.

units.leftText: If he comes in by himself, he shall go out by himself. If he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.
units.rightText: If he come in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he be married, then his wife shall go out with him.

units.leftText: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.
units.rightText: If his master give him a wife and she bear him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.

units.leftText: But if the servant shall plainly say, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children. I will not go out free;’
units.rightText: But if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free:

units.leftText: then his master shall bring him to God, and shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.
units.rightText: then his master shall bring him unto God, and shall bring him to the door, or unto the door-post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl; and he shall serve him for ever.

units.leftText: “If a man sells his daughter to be a female servant, she shall not go out as the male servants do.
units.rightText: And if a man sell his daughter to be a maid-servant, she shall not go out as the men-servants do.

units.leftText: If she doesn’t please her master, who has married her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.
units.rightText: If she please not her master, who hath espoused her to himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her unto a foreign people he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.

units.leftText: If he marries her to his son, he shall deal with her as a daughter.
units.rightText: And if he espouse her unto his son, he shall deal with her after the manner of daughters.

units.leftText: If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights.
units.rightText: If he take him another wife; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish.

units.leftText: If he doesn’t do these three things for her, she may go free without paying any money.
units.rightText: And if he do not these three things unto her, then shall she go out for nothing, without money.

units.leftText: “One who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death,
units.rightText: He that smiteth a man, so that he dieth, shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: but not if it is unintentional, but God allows it to happen; then I will appoint you a place where he shall flee.
units.rightText: And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.

units.leftText: If a man schemes and comes presumptuously on his neighbor to kill him, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.
units.rightText: And if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbor, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.

units.leftText: “Anyone who attacks his father or his mother shall be surely put to death.
units.rightText: And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.

units.leftText: “Anyone who kidnaps someone and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
units.rightText: And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: “Anyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
units.rightText: And he that curseth his father or his mother, shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: “If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he doesn’t die, but is confined to bed;
units.rightText: And if men contend, and one smite the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he die not, but keep his bed;

units.leftText: if he rises again and walks around with his staff, then he who struck him shall be cleared; only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall provide for his healing until he is thoroughly healed.
units.rightText: if he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote him be quit: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed.

units.leftText: “If a man strikes his servant or his maid with a rod, and he dies under his hand, the man shall surely be punished.
units.rightText: And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, with a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall surely be punished.

units.leftText: Notwithstanding, if his servant gets up after a day or two, he shall not be punished, for the servant is his property.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding, if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished: for he is his money.

units.leftText: “If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be surely fined as much as the woman’s husband demands and the judges allow.
units.rightText: And if men strive together, and hurt a woman with child, so that her fruit depart, and yet no harm follow; he shall be surely fined, according as the woman’s husband shall lay upon him; and he shall pay as the judges determine.

units.leftText: But if any harm follows, then you must take life for life,
units.rightText: But if any harm follow, then thou shalt give life for life,

units.leftText: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
units.rightText: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

units.leftText: burning for burning, wound for wound, and bruise for bruise.
units.rightText: burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

units.leftText: “If a man strikes his servant’s eye, or his maid’s eye, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.
units.rightText: And if a man smite the eye of his servant, or the eye of his maid, and destroy it; he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.

units.leftText: If he strikes out his male servant’s tooth, or his female servant’s tooth, he shall let the servant go free for his tooth’s sake.
units.rightText: And if he smite out his man-servant’s tooth, or his maid-servant’s tooth, he shall let him go free for his tooth’s sake.

units.leftText: “If a bull gores a man or a woman to death, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible.
units.rightText: And if an ox gore a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be surely stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be quit.

units.leftText: But if the bull had a habit of goring in the past, and this has been testified to its owner, and he has not kept it in, but it has killed a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death.
units.rightText: But if the ox was wont to gore in time past, and it hath been testified to its owner, and he hath not kept it in, but it hath killed a man or a woman; the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.

units.leftText: If a ransom is imposed on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed.
units.rightText: If there be laid on him a ransom, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatsoever is laid upon him.

units.leftText: Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.
units.rightText: Whether it have gored a son, or have gored a daughter, according to this judgment shall it be done unto him.

units.leftText: If the bull gores a male servant or a female servant, thirty shekels of silver shall be given to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.
units.rightText: If the ox gore a man-servant or a maid-servant, there shall be given unto their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
leftNotes: 21:32 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 30 shekels is about 300 grams or about 10.6 ounces.

units.leftText: “If a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and doesn’t cover it, and a bull or a donkey falls into it,
units.rightText: And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit and not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall therein,

units.leftText: the owner of the pit shall make it good. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
units.rightText: the owner of the pit shall make it good; he shall give money unto the owner thereof, and the dead beast shall be his.

units.leftText: “If one man’s bull injures another’s, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live bull, and divide its price; and they shall also divide the dead animal.
units.rightText: And if one man’s ox hurt another’s, so that it dieth, then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the price of it; and the dead also they shall divide.

units.leftText: Or if it is known that the bull was in the habit of goring in the past, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall surely pay bull for bull, and the dead animal shall be his own.
units.rightText: Or if it be known that the ox was wont to gore in time past, and its owner hath not kept it in; he shall surely pay ox for ox, and the dead beast shall be his own.

units.leftText: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it or sells it, he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
units.rightText: If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

units.leftText: If the thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no guilt of bloodshed for him.
units.rightText: If the thief be found breaking in, and be smitten so that he dieth, there shall be no bloodguiltiness for him.

units.leftText: If the sun has risen on him, he is guilty of bloodshed. He shall make restitution. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
units.rightText: If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be bloodguiltiness for him; he shall make restitution: if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.

units.leftText: If the stolen property is found in his hand alive, whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.
units.rightText: If the theft be found in his hand alive, whether it be ox, or ass, or sheep, he shall pay double.

units.leftText: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be eaten by letting his animal loose, and it grazes in another man’s field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field, and from the best of his own vineyard.
units.rightText: If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall let his beast loose, and it feed in another man’s field; of the best of his own field, and of the best of his own vineyard, shall he make restitution.

units.leftText: “If fire breaks out, and catches in thorns so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; he who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
units.rightText: If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.

units.leftText: “If a man delivers to his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it is stolen out of the man’s house, if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
units.rightText: If a man shall deliver unto his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief be found, he shall pay double.

units.leftText: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out whether or not he has put his hand on his neighbor’s goods.
units.rightText: If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shall come near unto God, to see whether he have not put his hand unto his neighbor’s goods.

units.leftText: For every matter of trespass, whether it is for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for clothing, or for any kind of lost thing, about which one says, ‘This is mine,’ the cause of both parties shall come before God. He whom God condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.
units.rightText: For every matter of trespass, whether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, or for any manner of lost thing, whereof one saith, This is it, the cause of both parties shall come before God; he whom God shall condemn shall pay double unto his neighbor.

units.leftText: “If a man delivers to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies or is injured, or driven away, no man seeing it;
units.rightText: If a man deliver unto his neighbor an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast, to keep; and it die, or be hurt, or driven away, no man seeing it:

units.leftText: the oath of the LORD shall be between them both, he has not put his hand on his neighbor’s goods; and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.
units.rightText: the oath of Jehovah shall be between them both, whether he hath not put his hand unto his neighbor’s goods; and the owner thereof shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.

units.leftText: But if it is stolen from him, the one who stole shall make restitution to its owner.
units.rightText: But if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner thereof.

units.leftText: If it is torn in pieces, let him bring it for evidence. He shall not make good that which was torn.
units.rightText: If it be torn in pieces, let him bring it for witness: he shall not make good that which was torn.

units.leftText: “If a man borrows anything of his neighbor’s, and it is injured, or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.
units.rightText: And if a man borrow aught of his neighbor, and it be hurt, or die, the owner thereof not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.

units.leftText: If its owner is with it, he shall not make it good. If it is a leased thing, it came for its lease.
units.rightText: If the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make it good: if it be a hired thing, it came for its hire.

units.leftText: “If a man entices a virgin who isn’t pledged to be married, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife.
units.rightText: And if a man entice a virgin that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife.

units.leftText: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
units.rightText: If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.

units.leftText: “You shall not allow a sorceress to live.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not suffer a sorceress to live.

units.leftText: “Whoever has sex with an animal shall surely be put to death.
units.rightText: Whosoever lieth with a beast shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: “He who sacrifices to any god, except to the LORD only, shall be utterly destroyed.
units.rightText: He that sacrificeth unto any god, save unto Jehovah only, shall be utterly destroyed.

units.leftText: “You shall not wrong an alien or oppress him, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And a sojourner shalt thou not wrong, neither shalt thou oppress him: for ye were sojourners in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: “You shall not take advantage of any widow or fatherless child.
units.rightText: Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.

units.leftText: If you take advantage of them at all, and they cry at all to me, I will surely hear their cry;
units.rightText: If thou afflict them at all, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry;

units.leftText: and my wrath will grow hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
units.rightText: and my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.

units.leftText: “If you lend money to any of my people with you who is poor, you shall not be to him as a creditor. You shall not charge him interest.
units.rightText: If thou lend money to any of my people with thee that is poor, thou shalt not be to him as a creditor; neither shall ye lay upon him interest.

units.leftText: If you take your neighbor’s garment as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,
units.rightText: If thou at all take thy neighbor’s garment to pledge, thou shalt restore it unto him before the sun goeth down:

units.leftText: for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What would he sleep in? It will happen, when he cries to me, that I will hear, for I am gracious.
units.rightText: for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin: wherein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.

units.leftText: “You shall not blaspheme God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not revile God, nor curse a ruler of thy people.

units.leftText: “You shall not delay to offer from your harvest and from the outflow of your presses.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not delay to offer of thy harvest, and of the outflow of thy presses. The first-born of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.

units.leftText: You shall do likewise with your cattle and with your sheep. It shall be with its mother seven days, then on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
units.rightText: Likewise shalt thou do with thine oxen, and with thy sheep: seven days it shall be with its dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.

units.leftText: “You shall be holy men to me, therefore you shall not eat any meat that is torn by animals in the field. You shall cast it to the dogs.
units.rightText: And ye shall be holy men unto me: therefore ye shall not eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs.

units.leftText: “You shall not spread a false report. Don’t join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not take up a false report: put not thy hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.

units.leftText: “You shall not follow a crowd to do evil. You shall not testify in court to side with a multitude to pervert justice.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to turn aside after a multitude to wrest justice:

units.leftText: You shall not favor a poor man in his cause.
units.rightText: neither shalt thou favor a poor man in his cause.

units.leftText: “If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again.
units.rightText: If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.

units.leftText: If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him with it.
units.rightText: If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt forbear to leave him, thou shalt surely release it with him.

units.leftText: “You shall not deny justice to your poor people in their lawsuits.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not wrest the justice due to thy poor in his cause.

units.leftText: “Keep far from a false charge, and don’t kill the innocent and righteous; for I will not justify the wicked.
units.rightText: Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.

units.leftText: “You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who have sight and perverts the words of the righteous.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take no bribe: for a bribe blindeth them that have sight, and perverteth the words of the righteous.

units.leftText: “You shall not oppress an alien, for you know the heart of an alien, since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And a sojourner shalt thou not oppress: for ye know the heart of a sojourner, seeing ye were sojourners in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: “For six years you shall sow your land, and shall gather in its increase,
units.rightText: And six years thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in the increase thereof:

units.leftText: but the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, that the poor of your people may eat; and what they leave the animal of the field shall eat. In the same way, you shall deal with your vineyard and with your olive grove.
units.rightText: but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie fallow; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave the beast of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy oliveyard.

units.leftText: “Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, that your ox and your donkey may have rest, and the son of your servant, and the alien may be refreshed.
units.rightText: Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest; that thine ox and thine ass may have rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the sojourner, may be refreshed.

units.leftText: “Be careful to do all things that I have said to you; and don’t invoke the name of other gods or even let them be heard out of your mouth.
units.rightText: And in all things that I have said unto you take ye heed: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.

units.leftText: “You shall observe a feast to me three times a year.
units.rightText: Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.

units.leftText: You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it you came out of Egypt), and no one shall appear before me empty.
units.rightText: The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep: seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it thou camest out from Egypt); and none shall appear before me empty:

units.leftText: And the feast of harvest, the first fruits of your labors, which you sow in the field; and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, when you gather in your labors out of the field.
units.rightText: and the feast of harvest, the first-fruits of thy labors, which thou sowest in the field: and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, when thou gatherest in thy labors out of the field.

units.leftText: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: “You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread. The fat of my feast shall not remain all night until the morning.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the fat of my feast remain all night until the morning.

units.leftText: You shall bring the first of the first fruits of your ground into the house of the LORD your God.
units.rightText: The first of the first-fruits of thy ground thou shalt bring into the house of Jehovah thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.

units.leftText: “Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
units.rightText: Behold, I send an angel before thee, to keep thee by the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.

units.leftText: Pay attention to him, and listen to his voice. Don’t provoke him, for he will not pardon your disobedience, for my name is in him.
units.rightText: Take ye heed before him, and hearken unto his voice; provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgression: for my name is in him.

units.leftText: But if you indeed listen to his voice, and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries.
units.rightText: But if thou shalt indeed hearken unto his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.

units.leftText: For my angel shall go before you, and bring you in to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I will cut them off.
units.rightText: For mine angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite: and I will cut them off.

units.leftText: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor follow their practices, but you shall utterly overthrow them and demolish their pillars.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works; but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and break in pieces their pillars.

units.leftText: You shall serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will take sickness away from among you.
units.rightText: And ye shall serve Jehovah your God, and he will bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.

units.leftText: No one will miscarry or be barren in your land. I will fulfill the number of your days.
units.rightText: There shall none cast her young, nor be barren, in thy land: the number of thy days I will fulfil.

units.leftText: I will send my terror before you, and will confuse all the people to whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
units.rightText: I will send my terror before thee, and will discomfit all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.

units.leftText: I will send the hornet before you, which will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before you.
units.rightText: And I will send the hornet before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.

units.leftText: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the animals of the field multiply against you.
units.rightText: I will not drive them out from before thee in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the field multiply against thee.

units.leftText: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.
units.rightText: By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.

units.leftText: I will set your border from the Red Sea even to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.
units.rightText: And I will set thy border from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness unto the River: for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand: and thou shalt drive them out before thee.

units.leftText: You shall make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
units.rightText: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.

units.leftText: They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against me, for if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
units.rightText: They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me; for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.

units.leftText: He said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD, you, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship from a distance.
units.rightText: And he said unto Moses, Come up unto Jehovah, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship ye afar off:

units.leftText: Moses alone shall come near to the LORD, but they shall not come near. The people shall not go up with him.”
units.rightText: and Moses alone shall come near unto Jehovah; but they shall not come near; neither shall the people go up with him.

units.leftText: Moses came and told the people all the LORD’s words, and all the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice, and said, “All the words which the LORD has spoken will we do.”
units.rightText: And Moses came and told the people all the words of Jehovah, and all the ordinances: and all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words which Jehovah hath spoken will we do.

units.leftText: Moses wrote all the LORD’s words, then rose up early in the morning and built an altar at the base of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: And Moses wrote all the words of Jehovah, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the mount, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.

units.leftText: He sent young men of the children of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of cattle to the LORD.
units.rightText: And he sent young men of the children of Israel, who offered burnt-offerings, and sacrificed peace-offerings of oxen unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
units.rightText: And Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basins; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.

units.leftText: He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and they said, “We will do all that the LORD has said, and be obedient.”
units.rightText: And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that Jehovah hath spoken will we do, and be obedient.

units.leftText: Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which the LORD has made with you concerning all these words.”
units.rightText: And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which Jehovah hath made with you concerning all these words.

units.leftText: Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.
units.rightText: Then went up Moses, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel:

units.leftText: They saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone, like the skies for clearness.
units.rightText: and they saw the God of Israel; and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of sapphire stone, and as it were the very heaven for clearness.
leftNotes: 24:10 or, lapis lazuli

units.leftText: He didn’t lay his hand on the nobles of the children of Israel. They saw God, and ate and drank.
units.rightText: And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: and they beheld God, and did eat and drink.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain, and stay here, and I will give you the stone tablets with the law and the commands that I have written, that you may teach them.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I will give thee the tables of stone, and the law and the commandment, which I have written, that thou mayest teach them.

units.leftText: Moses rose up with Joshua, his servant, and Moses went up onto God’s Mountain.
units.rightText: And Moses rose up, and Joshua his minister: and Moses went up into the mount of God.

units.leftText: He said to the elders, “Wait here for us, until we come again to you. Behold, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever is involved in a dispute can go to them.”
units.rightText: And he said unto the elders, Tarry ye here for us, until we come again unto you: and, behold, Aaron and Hur are with you: whosoever hath a cause, let him come near unto them.

units.leftText: Moses went up on the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
units.rightText: And Moses went up into the mount, and the cloud covered the mount.

units.leftText: The LORD’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. The seventh day he called to Moses out of the middle of the cloud.
units.rightText: And the glory of Jehovah abode upon mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days: and the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud.

units.leftText: The appearance of the LORD’s glory was like devouring fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: And the appearance of the glory of Jehovah was like devouring fire on the top of the mount in the eyes of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Moses entered into the middle of the cloud, and went up on the mountain; and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
units.rightText: And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount: and Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, that they take an offering for me. From everyone whose heart makes him willing you shall take my offering.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they take for me an offering: of every man whose heart maketh him willing ye shall take my offering.

units.leftText: This is the offering which you shall take from them: gold, silver, bronze,
units.rightText: And this is the offering which ye shall take of them: gold, and silver, and brass,

units.leftText: blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair,
units.rightText: and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair,

units.leftText: rams’ skins dyed red, sea cow hides, acacia wood,
units.rightText: and rams’ skins dyed red, and sealskins, and acacia wood,
leftNotes: 25:5 or, fine leather

units.leftText: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense,
units.rightText: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense,

units.leftText: onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.
units.rightText: onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate.

units.leftText: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.
units.rightText: And let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.

units.leftText: According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all of its furniture, even so you shall make it.
units.rightText: According to all that I show thee, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all the furniture thereof, even so shall ye make it.

units.leftText: “They shall make an ark of acacia wood. Its length shall be two and a half cubits, its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
units.rightText: And they shall make an ark of acacia wood: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
leftNotes: 25:10 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.

units.leftText: You shall overlay it with pure gold. You shall overlay it inside and outside, and you shall make a gold molding around it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, within and without shalt thou overlay it, and shalt make upon it a crown of gold round about.

units.leftText: You shall cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in its four feet. Two rings shall be on the one side of it, and two rings on the other side of it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in the four feet thereof; and two rings shall be on the one side of it, and two rings on the other side of it.

units.leftText: You shall make poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make staves of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.

units.leftText: You shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, wherewith to bear the ark.

units.leftText: The poles shall be in the rings of the ark. They shall not be taken from it.
units.rightText: The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.

units.leftText: You shall put the covenant which I shall give you into the ark.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony which I shall give thee.

units.leftText: You shall make a mercy seat of pure gold. Two and a half cubits shall be its length, and a cubit and a half its width.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a mercy-seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.

units.leftText: You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make them at the two ends of the mercy seat.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make two cherubim of gold; of beaten work shalt thou make them, at the two ends of the mercy-seat.

units.leftText: Make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. You shall make the cherubim on its two ends of one piece with the mercy seat.
units.rightText: And make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end: of one piece with the mercy-seat shall ye make the cherubim on the two ends thereof.

units.leftText: The cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces toward one another. The faces of the cherubim shall be toward the mercy seat.
units.rightText: And the cherubim shall spread out their wings on high, covering the mercy-seat with their wings, with their faces one to another; toward the mercy-seat shall the faces of the cherubim be.

units.leftText: You shall put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and in the ark you shall put the covenant that I will give you.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put the mercy-seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee.

units.leftText: There I will meet with you, and I will tell you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the covenant, all that I command you for the children of Israel.
units.rightText: And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy-seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.

units.leftText: “You shall make a table of acacia wood. Its length shall be two cubits, and its width a cubit, and its height one and a half cubits.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a table of acacia wood: two cubits shall be the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.

units.leftText: You shall overlay it with pure gold, and make a gold molding around it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, and make thereto a crown of gold round about.

units.leftText: You shall make a rim of a hand width around it. You shall make a golden molding on its rim around it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make unto it a border of a handbreadth round about; and thou shalt make a golden crown to the border thereof round about.

units.leftText: You shall make four rings of gold for it, and put the rings in the four corners that are on its four feet.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that are on the four feet thereof.

units.leftText: The rings shall be close to the rim, for places for the poles to carry the table.
units.rightText: Close by the border shall the rings be, for places for the staves to bear the table.

units.leftText: You shall make the poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold, that the table may be carried with them.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the staves of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold, that the table may be borne with them.

units.leftText: You shall make its dishes, its spoons, its ladles, and its bowls with which to pour out offerings. You shall make them of pure gold.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the dishes thereof, and the spoons thereof, and the flagons thereof, and the bowls thereof, wherewith to pour out: of pure gold shalt thou make them.

units.leftText: You shall set bread of the presence on the table before me always.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set upon the table showbread before me alway.

units.leftText: “You shall make a lamp stand of pure gold. The lamp stand shall be made of hammered work. Its base, its shaft, its cups, its buds, and its flowers shall be of one piece with it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made, even its base, and its shaft; its cups, its knops, and its flowers, shall be of one piece with it:

units.leftText: There shall be six branches going out of its sides: three branches of the lamp stand out of its one side, and three branches of the lamp stand out of its other side;
units.rightText: and there shall be six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:

units.leftText: three cups made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a flower; and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a flower, so for the six branches going out of the lamp stand;
units.rightText: three cups made like almond-blossoms in one branch, a knop and a flower; and three cups made like almond-blossoms in the other branch, a knop and a flower: so for the six branches going out of the candlestick:

units.leftText: and in the lamp stand four cups made like almond blossoms, its buds and its flowers;
units.rightText: and in the candlestick four cups made like almond-blossoms, the knops thereof, and the flowers thereof;

units.leftText: and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of the lamp stand.
units.rightText: and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, and a knop under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of the candlestick.

units.leftText: Their buds and their branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it one beaten work of pure gold.
units.rightText: Their knops and their branches shall be of one piece with it; the whole of it one beaten work of pure gold.

units.leftText: You shall make its lamps seven, and they shall light its lamps to give light to the space in front of it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make the lamps thereof, seven: and they shall light the lamps thereof, to give light over against it.

units.leftText: Its snuffers and its snuff dishes shall be of pure gold.
units.rightText: And the snuffers thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, shall be of pure gold.

units.leftText: It shall be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these accessories.
units.rightText: Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made, with all these vessels.
leftNotes: 25:39 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds or 965 Troy ounces

units.leftText: See that you make them after their pattern, which has been shown to you on the mountain.
units.rightText: And see that thou make them after their pattern, which hath been showed thee in the mount.

units.leftText: “Moreover you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim. You shall make them with the work of a skillful workman.
units.rightText: Moreover thou shalt make the tabernacle with ten curtains; of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim the work of the skilful workman shalt thou make them.

units.leftText: The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains shall have one measure.
units.rightText: The length of each curtain shall be eight and twenty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains shall have one measure.
leftNotes: 26:2 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.

units.leftText: Five curtains shall be coupled together to one another, and the other five curtains shall be coupled to one another.
units.rightText: Five curtains shall be coupled together one to another; and the other five curtains shall be coupled one to another.

units.leftText: You shall make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling, and you shall do likewise on the edge of the curtain that is outermost in the second coupling.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling; and likewise shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is outmost in the second coupling.

units.leftText: You shall make fifty loops in the one curtain, and you shall make fifty loops in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling. The loops shall be opposite one another.
units.rightText: Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling; the loops shall be opposite one to another.

units.leftText: You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains to one another with the clasps. The tabernacle shall be a unit.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains one to another with the clasps: and the tabernacle shall be one whole.

units.leftText: “You shall make curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make them.

units.leftText: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits: the eleven curtains shall have one measure.
units.rightText: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: the eleven curtains shall have one measure.

units.leftText: You shall couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shall double over the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tent.
units.rightText: And thou shalt couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shalt double over the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tent.

units.leftText: You shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outermost in the coupling, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which is outermost in the second coupling.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops upon the edge of the curtain which is outmost in the second coupling.

units.leftText: You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
units.rightText: And thou shalt make fifty clasps of brass, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.

units.leftText: The overhanging part that remains of the curtains of the tent—the half curtain that remains—shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.
units.rightText: And the overhanging part that remaineth of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.

units.leftText: The cubit on the one side and the cubit on the other side, of that which remains in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
